metadata.name: MTS 2019 Patient-Reportable Screening Knowledge Base
metadata.purpose: Preliminary emergency urgency screening from patient-reported or directly observable information while the user is travelling to or seeking a medical facility.
metadata.clinical_scope: Screening only; non-diagnostic; not a replacement for professional triage.

source_policy.note: Rebuilt from malaysiantriagescalenewrevised2019.pdf. Adult complaints-list columns are Levels 2-5; paediatric complaints-list columns are Levels 1-4; Critical First Look / Rapid Assessment columns are Levels 1-3. Criteria requiring measurements or clinician assessment are excluded from the active patient screening path (kept per rule under source_conditions_excluded_from_screening) rather than replaced with new thresholds.

screening_constraints.history_use: Use past medical history only when the applicable source rule explicitly makes the history relevant; do not independently escalate because of a diagnosis.
screening_constraints.insufficient_information_action: Ask only source-relevant follow-up questions; if classification remains unsupported, return insufficient_information rather than guessing.

limitations: This knowledge base is strictly for preliminary, non-diagnostic urgency screening by non-clinicians/patients.
It does not replace professional clinical triage, physical examination, ECG, laboratory tests, or diagnostic evaluation.
Clinician/measured criteria from the source are not part of the active self-screening decision path.
Australian Triage Scale (ATS) and other international triage rules are excluded from direct MTS mapping.
Generally, children, especially those below 8 years of age, should not be triaged at Level 5 (Routine); paediatric patients (under 12) may be triaged to Levels 1-4 as needed.

Only information a person can give by questionnaire or verbally is used. Criteria that need equipment, measurements or a clinician's examination or judgement are excluded (see excluded_from_active_screening).
The 'Referrals' complaint (ischaemic limb, vascular injuries, aortic aneurysms, febrile neutropenia) is not screened: every item is a clinician diagnosis.

assessment_modes.patient_reportable: Criterion can be obtained from the user's report or direct observation without equipment.
assessment_modes.excluded_clinician_only: Source criteria requiring measurements or clinician assessment are excluded from the active screening path.

patient_context.rule: Only use a history item as a triage modifier when the applicable MTS-derived rule explicitly supports that use.

instructions: Understand the user's reported symptoms and current condition.
Ask only additional questions necessary to evaluate applicable rules in this knowledge base.
Use patient-reported and directly observable information only.
Consider relevant past medical history when the source rule explicitly identifies it as relevant.
Do not invent, infer, interpolate, or substitute a medical triage rule.
Do not ask the user to obtain a vital sign or clinical measurement for this screening workflow.
When a source rule contains both reportable and clinician/measured criteria, evaluate only the reportable criteria retained in this KB.
When multiple applicable rules are present, select the highest-priority triage level (Level 1 is highest urgency).
If the available information does not support a classification, ask a source-relevant question or return insufficient_information; never guess.
Return the matched rule IDs and source basis.
After preliminary triage classification, the hospital-routing tool may be invoked.
Hospital routing must never modify the MTS-derived triage level.

source_references.relevance: Single source for all rules: Critical First Look, Rapid Assessment, Vital Signs, Complaints Lists (Adult & Paediatrics), Paediatric Assessment Triangle.

level_advice.purpose: Level-native patient advice. App copy derived from the source's time-to-treatment targets (p.2); not a source rule.

levels.1: Level 1 - Resuscitation (target time to treatment: immediate). Call 999 now (112 from a mobile phone). This needs emergency care right away.
levels.2: Level 2 - Emergency (target: under 10 minutes). Go to the nearest Emergency Department immediately.
levels.3: Level 3 - Urgent (target: under 30 minutes). Needs urgent medical assessment: go to an Emergency Department.
levels.4: Level 4 - Early Care (target: under 60 minutes). Needs medical care soon: go to an Emergency Department or a walk-in / urgent-care clinic.
levels.5: Level 5 - Routine (target: under 90 minutes). Not an emergency: a clinic or outpatient visit is suitable.

emergency_advice.purpose: Extra advice given IN ADDITION to the level advice when the condition is present, even if its level is below 1.
emergency_advice.rule: Level 1 always includes 'call 999'. These conditions add 'call 999 (112 from mobile)' at lower levels too.

items.advice: Call 999 now (112 from a mobile phone) for an ongoing seizure, in addition to going to the nearest Emergency Department.

applicability.population_field: Each rule and question carries population = 'all' | 'adult' | 'paediatric'.
applicability.age_rule: Paediatric = under 12 years; adult = 12 years and older. Rules for the other population are skipped.

question_condition_mapping.purpose: Helps the agent turn a person's answer into condition IDs. Adds no rules and changes no level; rules and conditions are unchanged.
question_condition_mapping.maps_to: On each question: a list of {when, condition_ids}. 'when' is the plain-language part of the question or answer option; 'condition_ids' are the <rule_id>.C<n> conditions it sets. Only IDs applicable to the patient's age are used.
question_condition_mapping.yes_no_questions: A 'No' (or a normal answer) means every listed condition is absent. A 'Yes' to a multi-part question means at least one part is present: ask which one and record only the part(s) the person confirms.
question_condition_mapping.age_derived: On a rule: {C<n>: {field, op, value}} marks a condition that is decided by age_years alone (present if the comparison holds, otherwise absent). Do not ask the person.
question_condition_mapping.unmapped_conditions: A condition that no question maps to must still be resolved from what the person has said; never assume it absent.

primary_triage_pass_criteria.purpose: Items the source lists under the 'Secondary Triage' column (no level). They mean no primary-triage danger sign and are NOT triage conditions.

source_alignment_notes: Where one source row repeats the same finding at two levels, the higher-urgency level applies (source: 'the higher triage level modifier should be selected', p.6). Lower duplicates are not repeated.
Normalcy qualifiers listed as separate bullets in one cell (e.g. 'Fully conscious' + 'Cannot take orally') are combined into one condition so the condition is not trivially true for every patient.

'Ongoing seizures' is Level 2 in every adult table (p.3, 10) and Level 1 in the paediatric list (p.17). Because people with a seizure should call 999 whatever the level, emergency_advice adds that advice at Level 2.

Chest pain (adult): the source lists 'on-going chest pain' (Level 2) and 'persisting mild pain' (Level 4) without saying how to tell them apart when ECG and risk assessment are unavailable. Per product decision, the Level 2 condition is 'On-going high (severe) chest pain' and the agent must ask whether ongoing pain is high, moderate or mild. For the same reason Level 3 'Onset > 6 H' is qualified 'with moderate pain (4-7)': otherwise any mild pain older than 6 hours would match Level 3 and the source's Level 4 'Persisting mild pain' could never apply. Resulting adult flow: high ongoing = Level 2, moderate = Level 3, mild persisting = Level 4. 'New onset < 6 H' and 'Profuse sweating' remain Level 2 as in the source. Paediatric chest pain is unchanged.

'Fever onset 3 - 6 days' appears at both Level 2 and Level 3 in the dengue rows, next to different modifiers; it is modelled as fever 3-6 days WITH the listed modifier (lethargy / near-fainting = Level 2; abdominal pain or persistent vomiting = Level 3). 'No warning signs' at Level 4 vs Level 5 is modelled the same way (with a risk modifier = Level 4; without = Level 5). Syncope 'Full recovery, no deficits' at Level 4 vs Level 5 likewise (Level 5 only with a history of previous syncope).
Acute stroke (< 3 H Level 2, > 3 H Level 3) is screened in the Altered Mental State / Seizures / Neurological category, not repeated under Lethargy & Weakness.
'Not responding to call' is Level 2 (Critical First Look) while 'Unresponsive' is Level 1 (Rapid Assessment, Conscious Levels); both are kept as separate conditions.
'Mild URTI symptoms' appears at Level 5 (p.9) and Level 4 (p.10) in the adult respiratory rows; the higher level (4) is used.

Paediatric Assessment Triangle Level 3 cells (alert, good tone, consolable, looking around) describe normal findings and are treated as 'no danger sign' (proceed to secondary triage), not as Level 3 triggers.

Criteria that a person cannot give by questionnaire or verbally are excluded: measurements (SpO2, BP, ECG, CRT, glucose, temperature), clinician-judged impressions ('Septic / Toxic', 'Toxic appearance', 'Septic appearance', 'Airway unprotected', 'Airway reflexes lost', 'Requires assisted breathing', 'Abnormal posturing', 'Appears unwell', 'Distracting pain', suspected / possible vascular injury, suspected intra-abdominal bleeding / ectopic / AAA, compartment syndrome, 'Airway threatened') and staff decisions ('Need for sedation', 'Need for restraint', 'Inter-facility transfers', 'Referred cases'). 'Likely / possible' impressions that a person can describe in plain words (e.g. likely rib fractures, possible pelvic injury) are kept.

Syncope Level 4 'Full recovery, no deficits' is qualified 'and no history of previous syncope' (product decision, approved). The source lists Level 5 as the same findings plus 'History of syncope' but never says Level 4 excludes it; without the qualifier a person with a previous syncope matches both and, because higher urgency wins, Level 5 could never be reached.

Patient-facing question wording (approved product decision, Oct 2026). Rule conditions and levels are unchanged; only how they are asked changed. Critical First Look starts with one tick-all-that-apply checklist (Q_CRIT_02A): trouble breathing, bleeding or injury, pale/bluish skin with cold peripheries, or none. An option that is not ticked rules out the items it `covers`; a ticked option `opens` its detailed list. Laypeople picking from long clinical lists over-selected Level 1 items (e.g. a cough read as 'abnormal breathing sounds'). 'No trouble breathing' also covers the breathing items repeated in the respiratory and paediatric lists (not observed-only signs such as retractions or nasal flaring). Clinical terms have lay descriptions: 'Abnormal breathing sounds' = harsh / high-pitched, gurgling or snoring noise with every breath, not a cough, phlegm or blocked nose; 'Incessant cough' = non-stop coughing fits without catching breath; 'airway intact' (wheeze) = able to talk normally. Questions whose options can co-exist are multi_select; options not ticked are absent. Multi-part yes/no questions became explicit option lists with none_answers so each answer maps to conditions without interpretation.

Trauma (approved product decision, Oct 2026): the PDF lists trauma as separate rows (Chest / Abdo Trauma, Trauma Head Neck, Trauma Limb, Fall, Wounds / Skin; p.7, 8, 10, 11 and paeds p.15-18). The KB keeps one rule per level, so questions now follow the rows: an injury-area checklist (Q_TRAUMA_00) opens each row's list, and a row not ticked rules out (covers) that row's items. E.g. pregnancy, anticoagulant use, high-risk mechanism and elderly come from the Chest / Abdo row only and are not asked for a limb injury. End-state items (Mild symptoms, Unlikely fractures, Mobilizing well, Low-risk mechanisms, No symptoms) are never ruled out by area. 'Elderly' (Chest / Abdo) is read as > 65 like elsewhere in this KB; it and the paediatric 'Child < 5' items are decided from age. Lay wording: 'Unlikely fractures' + 'Mild symptoms' = can still use it / bear weight and it does not look broken; 'Small bone fractures likely, moving fingers / toes' = might be a small broken bone (e.g. finger or toe) but can move fingers / toes; 'Proximal long bone fractures' = possible broken thigh or upper-arm bone; 'Amputation proximal to wrist' = arm or leg cut off above the wrist or ankle, 'Distal amputation' = finger, toe or part of the hand / foot; 'Limb injury / deformity' (Fall) = an arm or leg looks deformed or badly injured. Limb Pain / Swelling: 'Generalized oedema' = swelling all over the body, not only the painful area (a swollen injured ankle is not generalized oedema); 'Not able to bear weight' = cannot put any weight on the leg.
